findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the Zod safeParse wrapper object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. an object of the form `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Here the return value is assigned to `key` and written straight into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The stored credential therefore becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` instead of the Google token object, so `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail on the next use and the user's Google Calendar integration breaks permanently until re-installed. The value must be `...data` (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`).

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys and validates nothing useful
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the string `"[object Object]"` for both entries (a ZodString stringifies to `[object Object]`), so the object literal collapses to a single property named `"[object Object]"` of type number/unknown. The comment claims 'any property with a number is the expiry' but Zod cannot express that this way. Effectively the credential-sharing path only validates `access_token` presence and silently accepts responses with no expiry, so expired tokens will be stored and reused.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced by the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers (e.g. zoom, office365) persist the parsed data as the credential key, so a bogus refresh token is written to the DB, silently destroying the real refresh token stored previously and making future refreshes fail with invalid_grant. It also mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data` when `success === false`, which will throw since `data` is undefined (though the preceding throw usually prevents this).

findings.title: `prisma` used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file. This is a compile/runtime error (ReferenceError) that breaks every Salesforce calendar operation, since `getClient` is called in the constructor path.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh result is discarded; stale access token still used
findings.body: A refresh_token grant is now executed on every `getClient()` call (every service instantiation, even when the existing token is still valid — an unnecessary API round trip and rate-limit risk), but the returned connection is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old credential rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. The refresh therefore has no effect on the request that triggered it. It also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce is not actually covered by the credential-sync feature this PR adds.

findings.title: Sync endpoint always returns a fetch Response, incompatible with axios/SDK callers
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled, but several callers expect the shape produced by their own refresh function: zoho-bigin and zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.*` (axios response), hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object with `expiresIn`/`accessToken`. With syncing enabled these will read `undefined` and store broken credentials (or throw). The sync branch needs per-app normalisation or each caller must handle both shapes.

findings.title: Credential-sync request is sent unauthenticated and response status is never checked
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret / signature header (the PR introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` but does not use it here), so anyone who can reach the self-hoster's endpoint can request tokens for an arbitrary user id. There is also no `Content-Type` header for the URL-encoded body and no `response.ok` check, so error pages are passed downstream as if they were token responses.

findings.title: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where userId is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, which the helper treats as the Cal.com user id and forwards as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. This will request tokens for the wrong user (or a non-existent one). `refreshAccessToken` must receive and forward `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Wrong app slug "zoomvideo" sent to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: The Zoom app slug in the app store / credential records is `zoom` (see `createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom", ... })` in zoomvideo/api/callback.ts), but the refresh call passes `"zoomvideo"`. A self-hoster's endpoint keyed on the Cal.com app slug (and the `app-credential` webhook, which looks up `prisma.app` by slug) will not match, so Zoom token sync silently fails.

findings.title: Webhook handler has no method check and unhandled parse/decrypt errors
findings.body: `handler` accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without try/catch. Malformed bodies, a wrong encryption key, or a non-JSON plaintext throw and produce an unhandled 500 with a stack trace rather than a 400. Validate the method and return structured 400s.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality and no empty-secret guard
findings.body: The shared secret check uses `!==` on the header value, which is vulnerable to timing analysis; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally, if the header is absent `req.headers[...]` is `undefined`; this is only safe because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` requires the secret to be set, but that constant is a truthy string expression rather than a boolean, so any future refactor could allow `undefined === undefined` to pass.

findings.title: Diagnostic logging for failed Outlook token refresh removed
findings.body: The previous code logged the Zod error and the raw Microsoft response when the refresh token response did not parse. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` with no detail, making Outlook refresh failures much harder to diagnose in production.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
findings.body: The expression `process.env.A && process.env.B` yields `undefined`/`""`/the second string rather than a boolean, so the exported constant's type is `string | undefined`. Consumers use it in boolean contexts today, but the name implies a boolean and it would serialize oddly if ever returned from an API. Wrap in `!!`.
